text:
it's about a week at cern following someone round in physics, engineering or computing, and you apply to cern directly
the catch is they only take you if work experience is compulsory at your school and the school signs their trainee agreement, so that's what you're asking them. oh and a parent has to come with you, so dad's spreadsheet gets a geneva tab
feeling: glad they're actually looking at it rather than dodging it. just explain it plainly, a bit of cheek about dad, then let them send the email
feedback: Good amount of detail and conversation.

text:
off cern's job shadowing page. swap in who it's to and your name, then send it before you board

Subject: CERN job shadowing as work experience

Dear [name],

I'd like to apply for a job shadowing placement at CERN in Geneva, usually a week following a physicist or engineer. CERN only takes secondary school students where the placement is an obligatory part of their school programme, and the school has to sign CERN's traineeship agreement if the student is selected.

Could you let me know whether this could count as my formal Year 12 work experience, and whether the school would be willing to sign the agreement if I'm offered a place? CERN asks for applications at least two months before the start date, so it would help to know before I apply. A parent would come with me for the whole placement.

Many thanks,
[your name]
